Need support: letter written 20th century first half, from ruler of one country to another, delivered by an official nicknamed after body part by recipient.

R2: "It was written roughly six months after the author had come to power."

R3: "In it, the author refers to their country having regained a region."

R4: "What is the name of the region referred to?" It's a question requirement: need name of region.

C1: Letter from King Michael of Romania to President of US was transmitted under cover of memorandum dated March 5, 1945, from William J. Donovan, Director OSS.
C2: King Michael handed letter to an OSS officer in Bucharest with statement pleased to have opportunity to transmit views to President unofficially.

Need judge. We have no nickname after body part in claims. No "roughly six months after came to power". King Michael? Came to power? Not in claims. No region regained. No name of region. R1 partially? Let's parse. R1 has multiple material parts:
- A letter was written in first half of 20th century: C1 date March 5 1945 (cover memo) implies letter around? C1 says letter transmitted under cover memo dated March 5, 1945. That likely supports letter existed and first half? C1 says letter from King Michael to President. C2 says King Michael handed letter to OSS officer in Bucharest. It doesn't explicitly date letter but C1 cover memo date 1945, first half. C2 maybe letter handed to OSS officer. 
- from a ruler of one country to another: King Michael of Romania (ruler? claims say King Michael; likely ruler of Romania) to President of US (another country's leader? President). Supports.
- delivered by an official who was nicknamed after a body part by its recipient: C1 says transmitted under cover of memorandum from William J. Donovan, Director OSS. C2 says handed to OSS officer. No nickname after body part. "delivered by an official" maybe OSS officer/Director Donovan? But no nickname. So substantive part unsupported.
Thus R1 partially supported? It establishes letter from ruler to another and date. Material part nickname not. So partially_supported. Need supported_by C1, C2 perhaps. Does C1/C2 establish "letter was written first half" C1 date of cover memo, maybe yes. C2 no date. C1 King Michael as King of Romania to President. C1 says letter from King Michael to President, transmitted under cover memo. C2 handed letter to OSS officer. I think partially_supported. Need be strict: Does "King Michael" count as ruler? The claim says King Michael of Romania. A King is ruler. "President of the United States" another country? Romania vs US. Yes. Delivery by official? C2 says handed to OSS officer. C1 transmitted under cover memo by Donovan. But no nickname. So partial.

R2: no claim about came to power or six months. Unsupported. supported_by [].

R3: no claim about author refers to country regaining a region. Unsupported.

R4: asks name of region referred to. No claim identifies region. Unsupported. However R4 is question itself; if R3 unsupported, R4 unsupported. supported_by [].

Could R1 be unsupported? Let's consider definitions: partially if at least one substantive material part. It does establish letter from King Michael to President of US and date. That is substantive. So partial. Fine.
